tagesgeld.name: Savings
tagesgeld.summary: A home for reserves you may need at short notice, with interest that follows the market.
tagesgeld.detail: Savings accounts suit liquidity you want to keep available. Rates are variable and can change at any time; compare the stated rate with its validity period.
tagesgeld.risk: Variable rates may fall. Deposit protection depends on the partner bank and its national scheme.
considerations: Which bank holds the deposit?
How long is the promotional rate valid?
Which deposit protection scheme applies?

festgeld.name: Fixed deposits
festgeld.summary: Commit capital for an agreed period at an agreed rate — clarity in exchange for flexibility.
festgeld.detail: Fixed deposits pay a rate set at the outset for the full term. Early access is usually not possible, so match the term to when you will need the money.
festgeld.risk: Funds are generally locked until maturity. Inflation can erode real returns.
considerations: When will you need the funds?
Is interest paid annually or at maturity?
What happens at the end of the term?

flexgeld.name: Flex deposits
flexgeld.summary: A middle path: a fixed horizon with defined notice periods that let you step out if plans change.
flexgeld.detail: Flex deposits combine a planned rate with notice-based access. Read the notice period and any rate adjustment on early withdrawal carefully.
flexgeld.risk: Early withdrawal can reduce the interest earned. Notice periods delay access.
considerations: How long is the notice period?
How is the rate adjusted if you exit early?
Is the term renewed automatically?

anleihen.name: Bonds
anleihen.summary: Lend capital to an issuer in return for scheduled interest — understand who pays, and on what terms.
anleihen.detail: Assess the issuer's credit quality, sensitivity to interest-rate moves, maturity and secondary-market liquidity together. A scheduled coupon is not a guarantee.
anleihen.risk: Payments depend on the issuer. Selling before maturity may return less than invested.
considerations: Who is the issuer and how is it rated?
How does a rate change affect the price?
Can you sell before maturity?

aktien.name: Stocks
aktien.summary: Participate in the growth of businesses — with the price movement that ownership brings.
aktien.detail: Equities can grow with company earnings over long horizons but fluctuate considerably. Diversification and time horizon matter more than timing.
aktien.risk: Share prices can fall sharply. Dividends are not guaranteed. Total loss is possible.
considerations: How concentrated is your exposure?
Could you hold through a 30% drawdown?
What are the full costs of trading?

ipo.name: IPO access
ipo.summary: Subscribe to companies entering the public market — read the prospectus before the headlines.
ipo.detail: New listings have limited trading history. Allocation is not guaranteed, and first-day prices can move in either direction.
ipo.risk: Limited track record, potential lock-ups and pronounced volatility after listing.
considerations: Have you read the approved prospectus?
How is the offer price determined?
Are there lock-up periods?

gold.name: Gold
gold.eyebrow: A store of value with a long memory
gold.summary: Physical or securitised gold as a diversifier — no interest, but a long role in preserving wealth.
gold.detail: Gold pays no income and its price is set in US dollars, so currency moves matter. Storage, insurance and spreads add to the cost of ownership.
gold.risk: Prices can fall for extended periods. Currency effects apply for euro investors.
considerations: Physical bars or a securitised product?
Where and how is it stored?
What is the buy/sell spread?

rohoel.name: Crude oil
rohoel.summary: Oil exposure via futures-based products — driven by supply, demand and geopolitics.
rohoel.detail: Most retail oil products track futures, not the spot price. Rolling contracts can create returns that differ markedly from the headline price.
rohoel.risk: High volatility and roll costs. Not suitable as a core holding for most investors.
considerations: Does the product track spot or futures?
What are the roll costs?
How large a position makes sense?

gold.name: Gold
gold.description: The most widely held precious metal, traditionally used as a store of value and portfolio diversifier.

silver.name: Silver
silver.description: A precious and industrial metal; demand from solar and electronics makes it more cyclical than gold.

platinum.name: Platinum
platinum.description: Used in catalytic converters and jewellery; supply is concentrated in a few producing regions.

palladium.name: Palladium
palladium.description: A key input for petrol-engine catalysts, with prices sensitive to automotive demand.

bitcoin.name: Bitcoin
bitcoin.description: The first and largest crypto-asset by market value. Highly volatile and not deposit-protected.

ethereum.name: Ethereum
ethereum.description: A programmable blockchain network whose native asset powers smart contracts. Highly volatile.

faqs.q: Do I need an account to explore?
faqs.a: No. Every product page, the market overview and the calculator are open to everyone. An account is only needed once you want to keep documents and conversations in one place.

faqs.q: What does the calculator actually show?
faqs.a: A simple projection based on the figures you enter. It is an estimate for orientation, not an offer, and it does not account for taxes, fees or rate changes.
No. Market references are indicative and shown with their source and observation time. They are not executable prices.

faqs.q: What is useful to include in a first message?
faqs.a: Your goal, an approximate amount and time horizon, and anything you already know you want to avoid. That is enough to begin a sensible conversation.
